title: Koebe's Circle-Domain Conjecture
main_claim: Every domain G in the Riemann sphere is conformally equivalent to a circle domain, with no restriction on the complement. Theorem 1.1 settles Koebe's Kreisnormierungsproblem in full. The proof goes through a retained-test transfer and selection theorem (Thm 6.6). It controls countably many compatible test coordinates under finite circle-domain uniformization. Small barriers collapse the unmarked ends. For the marked ends, which are countably many, period-one stream coordinates combined with a Stokes estimate rule out any protrusion beyond the limiting disk.
coverage:
I read the full LaTeX of sections 00-06 in ~/hive_audit/src/math/preprints/Koebes-Circle-Domain-Conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections and skimmed section 07 (the hyperbolic-surface corollary). I re-derived the following steps by hand, without sympy.
(1) The quotient sphere and dust-disk lemmas.
(2) Generic level continua: the finite-length argument giving local connectedness, and the null trace-image criterion.
(3) The finite transfer theorem. This covers the staircase expectation E q_i = 1, the wedge-sum bound with the (m-1)h term, the h^2 E J -> 0 bound by dominated convergence, and the Markov selection. It also covers the descending-label construction of filling disks: the free and flagged singleton-component claim uses (P) only at one lattice level per distinct label, so it does not need (P) on a diagonal. It covers the rank-one energy density tr(g^-1 A) sqrt(det g) -> 2 sqrt(l1 l2), the Cauchy-Binet identity det A = sum |du_i ^ du_j|^2, and the oscillation sum <= 4h sqrt(J).
(4) Normalized compactness via the area theorem (bound 5R), and the end-component identification and trapping.
(5) Collar concatenation, removal of one jump level, and Steps 1-6 of the barrier theorem. This includes the conversion from gates to a penalty density, the band bound 4m(s), smoothing that preserves the bands, and the compatibility of the new barrier.
(6) The measure-family modulus duality: increasing unions, open neighbourhoods, the compact subfamily, and the separation argument. Also the uniform modulus lower bound c0 = (beta/(4 C_bar))^2, and the fusion lemma, where I checked the minimax finite split, the usc neighbourhoods and the tree mixture.
(7) Point avoidance (the log-log density), the removal of diffuse dust intersections in all three cases, and the four-path crossing bound 4(2 delta + (1+4C) delta^2) < 10^-4. Also the countable termination of the first selection and the collapse of unmarked ends by line payment.
(8) The generic level-intersection lemma, including the detour/sign argument; the compact simple-arc reduction; the stream coordinate (ray index, the intersection inequality, the Sobolev bound sqrt2 g_eta, the boundary measure dv|_C = beta, bands bounded by m_eta, and (P)); the Stokes estimate; both cases of the bad-pair exclusion; and the countable termination of the second selection.
I found no step that fails. The verdict covers the logic as read; none of it was machine-checked.
